title: Executable File Created In A Public Or Temporary Directory
detection_hypothesis: If tooling is staged before execution, a file creation event will record an executable extension written into a user-writable directory.

field_semantics.TargetFilename: Absolute path of the file that was created or modified.
field_semantics.Image: Absolute path of the executable backing the created process.

collection_prerequisites: File creation auditing is enabled (Sysmon Event ID 11 or equivalent).
User-writable directories are not globally excluded from collection.
expected_collection_gaps: File modification without creation may not raise an event.
Aggressive exclusion lists commonly remove temporary directories.
normalization_assumptions: TargetFilename is an absolute path including the file extension.
ingestion_differences: Some agents report short paths or device paths instead of drive letters.
retention_considerations: File creation telemetry is high volume; 30 days of hot retention is typical.
expected_volume: Moderate; expected to be triaged through correlation rather than individually.
false_positive_strategy: This is a staging signal with a large benign population. Use it as correlation input rather than as a standalone alert, and tune on the writing process image.
tuning_guidance: Exclude known installer and packaging images by full path. Do not exclude by file extension, because that removes the only content constraint in the rule.
test_strategy: Positive cases write an executable and a library into different writable directories. Negative cases cover a document file, a managed directory, and the filtered update agent.
author: Salvatore Mazzaglia
